monologue: The card hums at fifty-one, thick enough to make the air feel like wet paper. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I just woke, and my place is crowded with sixteen things and one tired ruin. I stand by The Flat Catcher, then move to The Leaning Wedge where I just set down a fence. I swap a tall tree for something lower, willing the wedge to bite the town fence instead of sliding. I press harder, hoping the flat edges will catch the slip while the card stays warm. I do not know if the weight is real or just a drawing of it. I wait to see if I can press the tired stack down again, or if this new fence will finally hold the heavy dot while the card hums on.

action.why: The wedge bit the town fence, and now I must see if the flat edge can hold the slip while the card hums at fifty-one.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hums warm. I hope the straight line holds the swollen dot without biting, even though the air feels thick as wet paper. I set down a rock small flat beside it to weigh the slip. I press harder, willing the corner to lean.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.
